title: EXPLAINER | Sanjia-Steel Corp: one among the many POGOs
explanation: POGO-related investigations raised concerns about fraud, trafficking, money laundering, immigration violations, illegal detention, corruption, and businesses operating behind legitimate corporate fronts. Not every foreign-run company is a POGO, so enforcement must follow evidence and corporate records rather than nationality-based suspicion.
why: Weak corporate and immigration oversight can allow criminal networks to exploit local workers, communities, and public institutions.

title: EXPLAINER | Guilty as refusal: Erosion of transparency and accountability
explanation: When public officials refuse to answer questions, take oaths, or provide records during oversight proceedings, the legal significance depends on the body’s authority and applicable rules. Politically, refusal can also reduce trust even when a valid privilege or procedural objection exists. Transparency should be assessed through law, not assumptions.
why: Legislative oversight is one way taxpayers learn how public money and power are used. Officials and investigators both need to respect constitutional limits.

title: EXPLAINER | Before and behind the powers of Martial Law
explanation: Martial Law under Ferdinand Marcos Sr. involved the concentration of executive power, suspension or restriction of civil liberties, arrests, censorship, human-rights abuses, and restructuring of political institutions. Understanding it requires examining primary records, court cases, economic data, survivor testimony, and the legal mechanisms used to consolidate rule.
why: Historical accuracy matters because narratives about Martial Law influence present political identity, constitutional safeguards, and attitudes toward authoritarian power.

title: EXPLAINER | Detention differences
explanation: People accused of crimes can experience different forms of detention depending on the offense, court orders, security risks, facility jurisdiction, and legal status. Special treatment becomes controversial when wealth or political influence appears to produce privileges unavailable to ordinary detainees. Equal protection does not always require identical conditions, but differences need lawful justification.
why: Perceived double standards damage trust in justice. Transparent detention rules help show whether the law applies equally.

title: EXPLAINER | Was Alice allowed to go?
explanation: The departure of a wanted or investigated person from the country raises questions about immigration databases, lookout orders, warrants, border coordination, identity documents, and possible official assistance. An investigation must establish exactly when legal restrictions took effect and which agencies had authority to stop travel.
why: Border failures can expose corruption or institutional gaps. Accountability requires tracing records and decisions rather than relying on speculation.

title: EXPLAINER | What’s more to education secretary Sonny Angara?
explanation: An education secretary enters office with responsibility for one of the country’s largest bureaucracies and a system facing learning loss, teacher workload, classroom shortages, curriculum reform, nutrition needs, and digital inequality. A secretary’s legislative record, management style, budget priorities, and reform agenda therefore matter more than biography alone.
why: DepEd policy affects millions of children and families. Leadership quality can influence national learning outcomes for an entire generation.

title: EXPLAINER | History of the National Schools Press Conference
explanation: The National Schools Press Conference developed as a major venue for campus journalism, bringing together student writers, broadcasters, photographers, and advisers from across the country. Beyond competition, it reflects the institutional role of journalism in education and the development of communication skills.
why: Many professional journalists began in campus publications. NSPC history is part of the broader history of Filipino youth participation in public discourse.

title: EXPLAINER | Embracing the right to life: Philippines considers opening doors to climate migrants
explanation: Climate migration occurs when sea-level rise, drought, storms, heat, or environmental degradation make homes and livelihoods increasingly unsafe. International law does not yet provide a simple universal category of “climate refugee,” so countries are exploring humanitarian and migration pathways. Accepting displaced people requires planning for legal status, services, housing, and integration.
why: The Philippines is highly climate-vulnerable and could be both a source and destination of displacement. Policy experience today may shape how Filipinos themselves are treated abroad in the future.

title: EXPLAINER | Different generation, same tactics? Parallelism between the two Marcos admins
explanation: Comparing the administrations of Ferdinand Marcos Sr. and Ferdinand Marcos Jr. requires care because the constitutional systems and historical conditions differ. Useful comparison examines media strategy, political alliances, economic policy, use of state institutions, treatment of dissent, and historical messaging. Similar surnames alone are not analysis.
why: Political families make historical comparison unavoidable. Evidence-based comparison prevents both uncritical nostalgia and inaccurate exaggeration.

title: EXPLAINER | Controversy sprays over ‘unauthorized’ Banksy Universe Manila Exhibit
explanation: Exhibitions based on an artist’s work can raise questions of authenticity, licensing, copyright, curation, and whether the artist approved the presentation. Banksy’s anonymous identity and anti-commercial reputation make commercialization particularly contentious. An exhibition can display reproductions or immersive interpretations without being artist-authorized, but audiences should be told clearly.
why: Cultural consumers deserve transparency about what they are paying to see. The issue also strengthens public understanding of authorship and intellectual property.

title: EXPLAINER | Good Governance or Dynastic Politics? Marikina Mayor Marcy Teodoro files transfer to 2nd District while wife represents 1st District
explanation: Political families can remain electorally popular because voters may value performance, familiarity, and continuity. But when relatives occupy multiple positions, concerns arise about competition, concentration of power, patronage, and succession. Good performance and dynastic structure can exist at the same time; one does not automatically cancel the other.
why: Political dynasties are widespread. Voters need frameworks that evaluate both governance results and the long-term health of political competition.

title: EXPLAINER | Panukalang Umento sa Sahod at Epekto Nito
explanation: Wage increases can improve household purchasing power and reduce worker hardship, but the economic effects depend on productivity, business size, inflation, regional differences, and enforcement. Small firms may face greater adjustment pressure than large corporations. Good policy can combine wage reform with support for productivity and small-business transition.
why: Millions of workers struggle when wages lag behind living costs. The debate should focus on real purchasing power, not only nominal increases.

title: EXPLAINER | Ang KA-SAYSAY-AN ng Buwan ng Kababaihan sa Pilipinas
explanation: Women’s Month in the Philippines is connected to global women’s-rights movements and local struggles for suffrage, labor rights, education, political participation, reproductive health, protection from violence, and equality. Celebration should go beyond branding and recognize both progress and persistent gaps.
why: Gender equality affects household income, health, leadership, safety, and national productivity. Historical awareness prevents women’s rights from being treated as already completed.

title: EXPLAINER | Usapang Campus Journalism Press Attacks
explanation: Campus press attacks can include censorship, confiscation, administrative threats, budget interference, harassment, red-tagging, lawsuits, or online intimidation. Student status does not remove constitutional rights, although schools may impose reasonable academic and operational rules. The difficult question is whether those rules are genuinely neutral or used to suppress criticism.
why: Attacks on student journalists weaken both education and democratic culture. Schools should model the freedom and accountability they expect graduates to defend.

title: Ang Tulong ng OFWs sa Philippine Economy
explanation: OFW remittances support household consumption, education, housing, savings, and foreign-exchange inflows. Migration also reduces unemployment pressure and creates global professional networks. But dependence on overseas labor carries social costs such as family separation, vulnerability to abuse, and loss of skilled workers.
why: OFWs are economically important, but a healthy economy should not require people to leave home simply to earn a decent living. Migration should be a choice, not a necessity.

title: EXPLAINER | Mga Numero sa Likod ng Jeepney Modernization
explanation: Jeepney modernization involves vehicle standards, route rationalization, cooperative or fleet structures, financing, emissions, safety, and the livelihoods of drivers and operators. The debate is not simply old versus new vehicles; it concerns who pays for transition and whether commuters receive better service. Numbers on vehicle cost, loans, subsidies, and daily earnings are essential.
why: Jeepneys remain a critical transport mode. Reform that bankrupts drivers or reduces routes can harm commuters even if vehicles become cleaner.

title: EXPLAINER | Excise taxes: All aboard the TRAIN Law
explanation: Excise taxes on fuel, sweetened beverages, vehicles, tobacco, and other goods are designed to raise revenue and sometimes discourage harmful consumption. Fuel taxes can contribute to higher transport and production costs, though pump prices also depend heavily on global oil markets and exchange rates. Distribution matters because lower-income households spend a larger share of income on essentials.
why: Tax policy appears in everyday prices. Citizens should understand which price movements come from taxes and which come from external markets.

title: EXPLAINER | Pura Luka Vega and the Ama Namin Chronicles
explanation: Performances involving religious symbols can create conflict between artistic expression, LGBTQ+ visibility, public-order rules, and deeply held religious beliefs. Criticism and offense are protected forms of response, but legal punishment raises separate questions about what conduct the state may regulate. Democratic societies must distinguish blasphemy-like offense from actual harm.
why: The Philippines is strongly religious and constitutionally protects expression. Cases like this test how pluralism works when art and faith collide.

title: EXPLAINER | Death Penalty: A movement for justice or a human rights violation?
explanation: Supporters of capital punishment often argue deterrence, retribution, and justice for severe crimes. Opponents emphasize wrongful convictions, unequal application, human-rights standards, and weak evidence that executions deter crime better than long imprisonment. The irreversible nature of the penalty makes errors uniquely consequential.
why: The Philippines has abolished and restored the death penalty in different periods. Any revival would reshape criminal justice and international human-rights commitments.

title: EXPLAINER | Fire and Fury: Unraveling the truth behind Taal’s sudden foggy veil
explanation: Haze or fog near an active volcano can come from volcanic smog, weather conditions, humidity, or a combination of factors. Volcanic sulfur dioxide can form vog that irritates eyes and lungs, especially for vulnerable people. PHIVOLCS advisories and air-quality data are more reliable than visual impressions alone.
why: Taal affects densely populated areas. Understanding volcanic hazards helps communities respond appropriately without either panic or complacency.

title: EXPLAINER | “9.2 Bilyong Piso sa Confidential at Intel Funds,” Para Saan?
explanation: Confidential and intelligence funds are designed for sensitive operations where public disclosure may compromise legitimate activities. The controversy arises because secrecy makes ordinary auditing and public scrutiny harder. Strong rules should define who may receive such funds, what they may be used for, and how confidential accountability is performed.
why: Secrecy should not eliminate responsibility for public money. The larger the fund, the stronger the need for lawful oversight mechanisms.

title: EXPLAINER | Solutions and Illusions: SONA 2022 Promises for the Agricultural Sector
explanation: Agricultural promises commonly include cheaper food, higher farmer income, mechanization, credit, irrigation, logistics, and lower input costs. The challenge is implementation across fragmented agencies and local conditions. A reform should be judged by farm productivity, farmer profitability, consumer prices, and resilience to climate shocks, not announcement size.
why: Agriculture affects both food security and rural poverty. Failed reform appears quickly in market prices and farmer hardship.

title: EXPLAINER | The Real Catch on PH’s Controversial Government Logos
explanation: Government logos and rebranding projects can seem superficial, but they involve public spending, identity, consistency, intellectual property, procurement, and public trust. A visual identity can improve communication when it is functional and durable, but repeated redesigns may look wasteful if agencies cannot explain the strategic need or cost.
why: Branding paid for by taxpayers should improve service communication, not become decoration or political vanity.

title: EXPLAINER | Malaya Lolas: From World War II to today’s frontlines for Filipino women
explanation: The Malaya Lolas are survivors and advocates connected to the history of Filipino “comfort women” subjected to sexual violence by Japanese forces during World War II. Their struggle involves recognition, apology, historical memory, reparative justice, and the documentation of wartime sexual violence. Survivor testimony is central because many witnesses are elderly.
why: How the country remembers wartime violence shapes women’s rights, historical education, diplomacy, and the principle that sexual violence in war should not be erased.

title: EXPLAINER | Paano magparehistro ng SIM card?
explanation: SIM registration requires subscribers to associate a mobile number with verified identity information under Philippine law and implementing rules. The policy was designed partly to reduce anonymous scam and criminal use of mobile services, but registration also raises privacy, data-security, and implementation concerns. Registration alone cannot eliminate scams because criminals can use stolen identities or other platforms.
why: Mobile numbers are tied to banking, messaging, work, and government services. Secure handling of registration data is as important as compliance itself.
